diagnostic_evidence.quote: For sound hard boundary conditions, we set $X \coloneqq H^2(\Omega)$
Let $u \in X$ be arbitrary and $u^{(i)} \in \mathbb{C}$ s.t. $u = \sum_{i \in \mathbb{N}} u^{(i)} e^{(i)}$.
For sound hard boundary conditions this follows from the assumption that $k^2 \not \in \{ \lambda^{(i)} \}_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem is stated for X = H^2_0 (sound soft) and X = H^2(Omega) (sound hard, impedance). For X = H^2(Omega) it is false: the proof expands u in the H^2_0-eigenfunctions of (EVP) and uses e(u,e_i)=lambda_i(u,e_i), which fails for u with nonzero trace (integration by parts leaves boundary terms; the form domain of the eigenproblem is H^2∩H^1_0), so (ATu,u) does not diagonalize. Moreover A cannot be T-coercive on H^2(Omega): for harmonic u_n with ||u_n||_{H^2}=1 and ||u_n||_{H^1}→0, (Au_n,v) is controlled by ||u_n||_{H^1}||v||_{H^1}, so ||Au_n||→0, contradicting boundedness below. The same sequence shows the full operators of (BFHard)/(BFImpedance) are not Fredholm. In addition, those forms contain (Δu, ∇v·ν)_{L^2(∂Ω)}, which is undefined for u∈H^2(Omega) (Δu∈L^2 has no trace), so lem:Kcompact's estimate via ||γ_0Δu|| is meaningless and γ_0Δ is in any case not compact; and the weak forms only encode one combined boundary condition, not both. lem:Ainjective's sound-hard part invokes the Dirichlet (H^2_0) eigenvalues, which are not the sound-hard resonances. On the discrete side, the impedance T_h is built from eigenfunctions of a subspace tilde X_h∩H^1_0 ⊊ X_h, so the expansion of u_h∈X_h in thm:DiscreteThCoercivity is impossible and A_h is not uniformly T_h-coercive on X_h.

failure_location.quote: The operator $A \in \mathcal{L}(X)$ defined by \eqref{eq:Aoperator} is T-coercive with respect to the $T$-operator defined in \eqref{eq:Toperator}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must reformulate the sound-hard and impedance problems on spaces incorporating the essential boundary condition (e.g. ∂_ν u = 0, resp. ∂_ν u = iθu) so that the boundary terms are well defined and the operator is a compact perturbation of a coercive one, introduce the corresponding (non-Dirichlet) eigenvalue problems and T-operators, restate the nonresonance condition in terms of those spectra, and redo the discrete impedance analysis accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: Well-posedness of the continuous and discrete problems with sound hard and impedance boundary conditions (for beta=0 and beta>0) is not established; the advertised existence/uniqueness and quasi-optimality for these cases rest on ill-defined forms and a false T-coercivity claim. The sound soft case is unaffected by this root.
issues.title: Sound-hard/impedance analysis on X = H^2(Omega): forms ill-defined, A not T-coercive (not even Fredholm), wrong spectrum for injectivity
issues.why_classification: Two of the three advertised boundary-condition regimes lose their well-posedness and convergence results; the resolution requires new formulations, new eigenproblems/T-operators and changed hypotheses, i.e. new proof architecture rather than a local fix.

issues.failure_explanation: Young's inequality gives the upper bound |(Δv,v)_{∂Ω}| ≤ (ζ/2)||Δv||² + (1/2ζ)||v||², not a lower bound, so the displayed inequality '0 ≥ positive sum' is an invalid inference; from Im a(v,v)=0 one only obtains a single scalar relation (moreover Im a(v,v) also contains Im(Δv,∂_νv)_{∂Ω} and the real part of (Δv,v)_{∂Ω}, which the paper omits), which does not force γ_0 v = 0 and γ_0 Δv = 0. The unique-continuation part therefore has no starting point, and injectivity of the impedance operator is unproven (for β=0 and β>0). This defect survives any repair of ISSUE-001 since it is an error in the argument itself.

issues.overall_effect: Uniqueness (hence, via the Fredholm argument, existence) for the impedance problem is unsupported; discrete impedance results relying on injectivity of the continuous operator (thm:vBZThm hypothesis) inherit this gap.
issues.title: Impedance injectivity proof uses Young's inequality in the wrong direction
issues.why_classification: The impedance uniqueness claim is central to the advertised well-posedness for that regime and the source offers no valid route to it; the correct conclusion (unconditional injectivity) may not even hold as stated.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Due to the regularity of the functions $u, v \in H^2_0(\Omega)$, we can swap the order of differentiation and integrate by parts to show that the last two terms in \eqref{eq:exp} are self-adjoint as well.

the eigenvalues $\{\lambda^{(i)} \}_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ of \eqref{eq:EVPBeta} are real, of finite multiplicity, and that the associated eigenfunctions $\{ e^{(i)} \}_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ form an orthogonal basis of $L^2(\Omega)$

issues.failure_explanation: The proof integrates by parts ignoring boundary terms, which only vanish if u and ∂_ν u vanish on ∂Ω; the paper's H^2_0 is H^2∩H^1_0, so ∂_ν u ≠ 0 in general. For constant n=(1,0) on the unit disc, u=1−r², v=(1−r²)x² (both in H^2∩H^1_0) give ∫(n^T H u n)Δv − Δu (n^T H v n) = ∫(u_xx Δv − Δu v_xx) = −2π ≠ 0, so (n^T H u n, Δv) is not symmetric and e(·,·) is not self-adjoint (the antisymmetric part is ∫_{∂Ω}(ξ·ν)(ξ·τ)[∂_νv ∂_τ∂_νu − ∂_νu ∂_τ∂_νv], nonzero also on polygons for directors not aligned with edges). Eigenvalues may be complex and eigenfunctions need not be L^2-orthogonal, so the T-operator (ToperatorBeta) and the eigen-expansion proof of thm:added-2 are unsupported; the discrete problem (EVPDisrbeta) with λ∈R is likewise non-symmetric. (The expansion (eq:exp) also has the wrong coefficient (n_x+n_y)² instead of n_x²+n_y² for ∂_x²∂_y²u.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Drop the self-adjointness claim and prove T-coercivity of A for β>0 by perturbation: use the β=0 operator T (thm:Tcoercivity on H^2_0) and require β smaller than the β=0 T-coercivity constant γ(k) divided by the continuity constant of the nematic term; adapt the discrete argument similarly.
issues.overall_effect: The T-coercivity analysis of the nematic (β>0) problem, continuous and discrete, lacks its foundation; realness of the spectrum and the definition of the nonresonance set for β>0 are unjustified.
issues.title: Nematic eigenvalue problem is not self-adjoint on H^2∩H^1_0
issues.why_classification: A contained perturbation argument recovers comparable well-posedness results for the nematic sound-soft case, but with a k-dependent smallness condition on β and a replaced proof, so the fix is more than local yet not a loss of the result.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds |e_h(u_h,u_h)| below by c(α||Δu_h||² + ||∇u_h||² + h^{-3}||u_h||²_{∂Ω}) and then asserts this is ≥ γ||u_h||²_ε, whose leading term is the full H^2-seminorm. In the sound-soft Nitsche case (ε=1, tilde X_h = X_h ⊂ H^2 with no boundary conditions) the inequality ||Δu_h||_{L^2} ≥ c|u_h|_{H^2} is false (discrete harmonic functions have Δu_h=0 and arbitrary H^2-seminorm); controlling |u_h|_{H^2} by ||Δu_h|| plus the penalized boundary term h^{-3}||u_h||²_{∂Ω} requires an elliptic-regularity/inverse-trace argument that the paper neither states nor proves. The same unproven step is reused in lem:added-3.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add and prove a norm-equivalence lemma |u_h|²_{H^2} ≤ C(||Δu_h||² + h^{-3}||u_h||²_{L^2(∂Ω)}) for u_h ∈ X_h (via H^2-regularity of the Dirichlet problem on convex/smooth Ω and an inverse estimate for the boundary trace), or weaken ||·||_ε to use ||Δu_h|| in place of |u_h|_{H^2} and restate the error estimates in that weaker norm.
issues.overall_effect: Uniform coercivity of e_h in ||·||_ε, hence uniform T_h-coercivity and the quasi-optimal H^2-type error estimates for the sound-soft Nitsche discretization, are not established as written.
issues.title: Discrete coercivity: ||Δu_h|| does not control |u_h|_{H^2} on X_h without boundary conditions
issues.why_classification: A contained new lemma (or a limited weakening of the norm in the estimates) resolves it without changing the overall method or main conclusions, but it is a genuine missing nontrivial argument rather than a local fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: one can construct an interpolation operator from $H^5(\Omega)$ to the Argyris finite element space that converges with rate $h^3$ with respect to the $H^2$-norm

issues.failure_explanation: For the degree-5 Argyris element the standard estimate is ||u − I_h u||_{H^2} ≤ C h^{3}||u||_{H^5} or ≤ C h^{4}||u||_{H^6}; the displayed bound with h^4 and ||u||_{H^5} is false (the h^4 rate needs H^6 regularity), and the surrounding prose contradicts itself (h^3 in the text vs h^4 in the display and the expected rate).

failure_location.quote: \Vert u - I_h u \Vert_{H^2(\Omega)} \le C h^4 \Vert u \Vert_{H^5(\Omega)}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace ||u||_{H^5} by ||u||_{H^6} in eq:interpolation (or change the rate to h^3) and make the prose consistent.
issues.overall_effect: Only the justification of the expected O(h^4) rate in the numerical section is affected; for smooth plane-wave solutions the expected rate is correct once H^6 regularity is used.
issues.title: Argyris interpolation estimate mismatches rate and regularity
issues.why_classification: A local correction of the regularity index restores a true statement without altering any conclusion.
